items.title: The car screen map is properly dark at night again
items.body: On CarPlay and Android Auto after dark, a medium-risk area could tint the whole map until it looked like the daytime map dimmed, washing out the roads. Medium-risk areas are now drawn lighter over the night map, so the map reads as night and the roads stay clear. Daytime is unchanged.

items.title: Closing a report map no longer forces a decision
items.body: In the report review screen, opening "View on map" left no way out except approving, rejecting, or force-quitting — the close button was being laid out underneath the details panel, off screen. It now sits at the top of every report map where you can actually reach it.

items.title: Starting a drive far from its start no longer ends it instantly
items.body: If a drive began while you were well away from the planned starting point, it could count as "arrived" the moment it started and stop before it began. It now re-routes from where you actually are and carries on, as it should.

items.title: Diagnostics tell memory in use from memory reserved
items.body: The diagnostics export and its heartbeat now record how much memory the app is actually using alongside how much it has reserved. The reserved figure was the one that looked like a leak in recent reports; the two numbers together settle that at a glance.

items.title: CarPlay mini map comes back after a music detour
items.body: On the CarPlay dashboard, switching to full-screen music and back could leave the Tsamaya mini map on its plain road-and-speed card, or show a blank tile for a few seconds while the map rebuilt. The map now stays ready while you are away and comes back already on your car. On phones where a long drive pushes memory high, the mini map also returns once things settle instead of staying hidden for the rest of the trip.

items.title: Route grades now explain themselves
items.body: A route card could show a worse grade than the one below it while listing fewer flagged areas, with nothing on screen to explain the gap. The missing piece was distance through low-risk areas, which counts towards the grade but was never shown. Route cards now say it, so the letter always matches what is listed.

items.title: Android phones now get updates too
items.body: Updates are published to Android as well as iPhone from now on, so both run the same version of Tsamaya. This one brings Android up to date with everything shipped since 16 August: honest traffic ETAs, the rebuilt route picker, background GPS that stops when the drive does, and the mid-drive time band fix.

items.title: CarPlay follows your car into night mode
items.body: When your head unit switches to night — a garage, a storm, early winter dusk — the car map now darkens with it instead of staying in daylight. Zone borders are also calmer on the night map, so your route stands out.

items.title: Road alerts reach the car screen
items.body: Reroute and heavy-traffic notices now show on CarPlay, closed roads draw their grey hatching there, and if barricades are reported on or near your route you get a heads-up as the drive starts.

items.title: Cleaner CarPlay chrome
items.body: The speed dial docks in whichever corner is free on your head unit, turn cards only take a risk colour when it matters (orange and red always, calmer tiers near the turn), reporting a speed camera is one screen shorter, and report confirmations dismiss themselves.

items.title: CarPlay route preview fixed
items.body: The route choices screen now frames your whole route beside the route card instead of behind it — on every head unit, whichever side the card sits. The car marker, speed dial and road pill no longer cover the preview, and the map uses the full visible space.

items.title: No more background battery drain after a drive
items.body: If a drive ended while your phone was locked, the app could keep using GPS in the background until it was force-closed — showing up as "Background Location Services" and real battery drain days later. Location now switches off the moment a drive ends or the app leaves the screen without one, and any stuck session from an older version is cleaned up when you next open the app. Guidance with the screen off during an actual drive is unchanged.

items.title: The route screen always shows your real choices
items.body: When Fastest, Balanced and Lower-risk all pick the same road, that card now says so in its title ("Fastest · Balanced · Lower-risk") instead of showing one unexplained route. And when other sensible roads exist, they appear as extra options — named by their main road, safety-graded, and fully drivable — on the phone and on the CarPlay picker. If there truly is only one sensible road, the screen says that too.

items.title: Pick Fastest, Balanced or Lower-risk on every trip
items.body: The route options are now named for the trade they make: Fastest takes the quickest way and makes no attempt to avoid flagged areas, while Balanced and Lower-risk steer around them. The Fastest card says plainly when it passes high-risk areas, with a one-time note the first time you choose it. The same three options, with the same wording, appear on the CarPlay route picker.

items.title: ETAs now belong to the route you actually chose
items.body: When your chosen route was not the road Mapbox considered fastest in traffic, the ETA could show that other road’s time and read minutes off from the very start of the drive. Every option now shows its own live-traffic ETA, and after a mid-drive reroute the ETA keeps its traffic adjustment instead of turning optimistic.

items.title: Zoom and pan the CarPlay map
items.body: The CarPlay route screen now has zoom buttons, responds to pinch and drag on touch screens, and redraws the map as you flip between route options. Panning while driving no longer overshoots, and the map returns to following the car a few seconds after you stop exploring.

items.title: Search for a new destination mid-drive on CarPlay
items.body: A Search button now sits in the CarPlay top bar while navigating. Pick a new place and the route options preview over your current drive — guidance carries on until you tap Go, and cancelling changes nothing.

items.title: Risk timing no longer freezes mid-drive
items.body: On long drives the app could keep using daytime risk levels after 17:30 (and evening levels after 19:30), so areas whose risk rises after dark were shown and priced too low. The time of day now updates reliably during navigation, including on CarPlay.

items.title: Evening and night risk levels restored for 221 areas
items.body: Some areas had their per-time-of-day risk levels stored in a format the app skipped, so they showed their daytime level all day. Those levels now load correctly.

items.title: Turning voice on mid-drive now tells you the right distance
items.body: Switching voice guidance on partway through a drive used to replay the last turn announcement with its old distance ("in 3 km" when the turn was 2.4 km away). It now announces the next turn with the live distance instead.

items.title: Music no longer dips seconds before the voice speaks
items.body: Natural-voice prompts are now downloaded and kept on the phone ahead of time, so the music ducks as the voice starts — not three seconds before it, and prompts no longer arrive late at the turn.

items.title: CarPlay shows rated areas it used to leave blank
items.body: On the car screen, yellow areas were drawn so faintly in daylight they looked like missing data, and verified-safe areas were not drawn at all. Yellow is now clearly visible and verified-safe areas show as a light green tint.

items.title: Guided tour highlights line up on Android
items.body: On Android the short tour that points out the navigation buttons was drawing its highlight slightly above the button it was describing. The highlight now sits on the right button.

items.title: Roads that are closed are now routed around
items.body: Some roads are gated off, barricaded or washed away, and map data is often years behind. Tsamaya can now hold its own record of those, plan around them rather than merely treating them as risky, and draw them greyed out with a hatch so they read as “not a road you can use” instead of as a danger area. A closed road is never counted as a safety warning, and if a closure sits between you and your destination you still get a route, with the road named so the barrier is not a surprise.

items.title: Saved places open properly again
items.body: Tapping a saved place from the Saved Places list used to stack a second copy of the home screen in front of the one that had taken your destination — so the map just slid back to where you were standing and nothing else happened. It now returns to the home screen you came from, with the place set and ready to Go.

items.title: Your car is back on the CarPlay mini map
items.body: The mini map decides on connect whether it can draw a live map, and a busy first connect could make it give up too early and hand the tile to the simpler backup map — which only ever drew a plain arrow, never your chosen car. The check now ignores time the phone spent frozen, the backup map draws your car too, and after the mini map steps aside to save memory it comes back as a map rather than a black rectangle.

items.title: Rerouting now follows your lead
items.body: When you keep choosing your own road, Tsamaya stops arguing. After a couple of quick reroutes it plans along the road you are actually driving — with a notice on screen — and your chosen safety level takes over again once you are back on a planned route. Risk colours and alerts stay honest the whole time. Auto-reroute also can no longer run out for the rest of a drive: the old hard cap of eight reroutes per trip (one tester hit it in 14 minutes) is now a rolling budget that always recovers, and it says so on screen on the rare occasion it pauses.

items.title: Alerts stick to your chosen voice
items.body: Safety alerts are spoken from a warmed-up cache now, so the natural Google voice keeps working at exactly the busy moments — like right after a reroute — where it used to briefly fall back to the plain iOS voice. The little spoken confirmations when you tap the voice button ("Alerts only") also use your selected voice instead of the system default. When a fallback does still happen, the app now records it so we can see how often.

items.title: Steadier on long drives
items.body: On phones with less memory, a long CarPlay drive could quietly end navigation mid-trip. Tsamaya now watches its own memory and temporarily switches off the decorative extras (3D buildings, the animated route line — never the safety colours) before that can happen, and brings them back once things settle. Risk-area voice alerts also remember their recent history across an app restart, so a restart mid-drive no longer repeats a warning you just heard.

items.title: Shared live-trip links now open inside Tsamaya
items.body: Opening a shared "track my trip" link on a phone that has Tsamaya installed used to land on the home screen with the trip nowhere in sight — the app claimed the link but only knew the web address under a slightly different name. Those links now open the live-trip viewer directly. Links opened on phones without the app keep working in the browser exactly as before, and older links your contacts already have are covered too.

items.title: See a proposed road closure on the map before approving it
items.body: The closure review queue now has a "See it on the map" button showing exactly which stretches of road would be marked red, and the area around them, before you approve anything. The watch already worked these out from OpenStreetMap while checking each closure and then discarded them; it now keeps them. Review team only.

items.title: Road-closure alerts now open the closures themselves
items.body: Tapping the daily "closures awaiting your approval" notification opened the app on the map with nothing to act on. It now opens a review queue showing each closure the watch found but would not publish on its own — the roads, the time window, the source, and why it was held back — with Approve and Reject. Approving publishes it on the next check, within 30 minutes. Review team only.

items.title: Voice prompts no longer weaken locked-phone navigation
items.body: The silent audio loop that keeps navigation running while the phone is locked was being torn down and rebuilt after spoken instructions — on a guided CarPlay drive that happened every few minutes, each time opening a brief gap in which iOS could pause the app. Handing your music back after a prompt now resumes the loop in place instead of rebuilding it. Also fixed the drive log recording the previous route’s remaining distance right after a reroute (display was always correct — only diagnostics were affected).

items.title: Dashboard mini map recovers after memory pressure
items.body: When iPhone memory ran low, the CarPlay dashboard mini map was switched off for the rest of the day as a protective measure — even unplugging CarPlay could not bring it back. It now returns on its own once memory has been calm for ten minutes, and comes back in the lighter map style so the retry does not recreate the pressure.

items.title: Reroutes no longer wait for your screen
items.body: Fixed a serious bug where a mid-drive reroute (and other live updates) could stall until the phone screen was woken — on locked-phone CarPlay drives, finished network responses were stuck behind iOS’s frozen JS timers. Rerouting now completes with the screen off, and a genuinely stuck reroute cancels itself and retries instead of silently switching off for the rest of the drive.

items.title: Warning border now matches the map in overlapping zones
items.body: Where a smaller, more specific zone sits on top of a bigger one, the screen-edge warning and risk alerts now follow the same “most specific zone wins” rule as the map colours and the router — no more red border while the map under the car shows orange.

items.title: Speed cameras and hotspots on the CarPlay map
items.body: The car screen now shows the same fixed speed-camera pins and hijacking / smash-and-grab hotspot markers as the phone maps, following the same Settings toggles.

items.title: Music dims only when the voice actually speaks
items.body: The music used to dip while the natural voice was still being fetched — a few silent seconds before anything was said. It now dims at the moment the words start.

items.title: Traffic heads-up now says it clearly
items.body: Routes are planned with live traffic, so a jam’s delay is already inside your ETA. The heads-up now says exactly that, instead of sounding like your arrival time is about to jump.

items.title: Reroutes and the speedo stay live with the screen locked
items.body: Coming to a stop with the phone locked used to freeze the app’s engine — reroutes could take minutes to land on CarPlay and the speedometer stuck at your last moving speed. Navigation now keeps itself scheduled through standstills, so reroutes, the speedo and safety updates stay current without waking the phone.

items.title: Forgotten trips end themselves
items.body: Parking just short of your destination (or pocketing the phone while the trip-rating card was up) used to leave navigation — and GPS — running in the background all night. A stationary, unattended trip now ends itself within half an hour, and the rating card steps aside when you leave the app.

items.title: CarPlay taps before GPS is ready now start themselves
items.body: Choosing a destination on CarPlay right after plugging in used to ask you to try again once GPS locked. The tap is now remembered and the route starts on its own the moment a fix lands. The branded Tsamaya car marker is also now correctly reserved on the car screen — everyone else gets the standard arrow or their own custom car photo.

items.title: Risk alerts stop repeating themselves
items.body: Driving along the edge of a risk area — or through the gap between two — could speak "entering a high-risk area" every few seconds. The alert now waits until you are genuinely inside an area, and the same level of risk stays quiet for two minutes after you leave it. The map, the route ribbon and the CarPlay tile still show live risk every second — only the voice and buzz calm down.

items.title: CarPlay mini map now shades risk areas
items.body: The small dashboard map (the one beside your music) only showed a coloured frame around the tile. It now shades the suburbs around you with the same colours as the full-screen car map.

items.title: Risk areas no longer double up on the map
items.body: Where two risk areas covered the same ground — a suburb sitting inside a larger area, or the same place listed under two metros — their colours were painted on top of each other, so a yellow area inside another yellow area came out looking a shade worse than either really is. Each patch of ground is now shaded once, in the colour the routing actually uses, with outlines still marking every area. The counts on the home screen no longer count one place twice either.

items.title: Search now finds the closest branch
items.body: Searching a place with a lot of branches used to offer them in no particular order — a Kung-Fu Kitchen or a Steers halfway across the province could come up while the one down the road never appeared. Suggestions are now weighted to where you actually are, and each one shows how far away it is as you type.

items.title: A proper search screen
items.body: Tapping “Where to?” now opens a full-screen search — recent trips up front, suggestions as you type, and a full results list with addresses, distance from you, ratings and open/closed status. Tap a place and you’re routing.

items.title: Over-speed chime
items.body: Opt in under Settings › Navigation › Speed warnings and Tsamaya plays a short ping when you drift more than 10 or 20 km/h over the posted limit, with an occasional reminder if you stay over. Off by default — and where no limit is known, nothing sounds.

items.title: Choose how camera alerts speak
items.body: Settings › Navigation › Speed cameras now has a voice-alert mode: every camera ahead (as before), only when you’re near the camera’s limit — about 8 seconds out, with a “check your speed” nudge — or off, keeping the map pins without the voice.

items.title: CarPlay keeps your voice and safety settings
items.body: When a drive started from the car screen with your phone still locked in your pocket, Tsamaya could fall back to the default guidance voice, volume and safety alerts instead of the ones you chose. CarPlay now loads all your saved choices — voice, volume, safety nudges, route preference and camera alerts — on every start.

items.title: Road-closure alerts, if you want them
items.body: Tsamaya can now tell you when a protest, race or road closure hits your city — the same disruptions it already routes you around. Alerts only go to the metro they affect, so you won’t be woken about a road 1,400 km away. A second, separate switch covers occasional new-feature news, so muting one never mutes the other. Both live in Settings › General › Notifications, and nothing is sent unless you allow it.

items.title: Reported speed traps stay honest about what they are
items.body: A camera van someone reported is now always treated as a van — shown for about three hours from when it was spotted, never turned into a permanent camera on the map. Only genuinely fixed cameras stay put.

items.title: Tell us when a switched-off camera comes back
items.body: Tap any greyed-out speed camera and you can now report that it’s working again — a few reports switch it back to a live camera. We also corrected one camera on Grayston Drive in Sandton that was wrongly left marked as active.

items.title: Johannesburg speed cameras marked as not operating
items.body: Johannesburg’s automated speed cameras have been switched off since December 2025 — the city’s contract with its camera supplier ended and the equipment was removed. Those cameras now show greyed out on the map, and tapping one explains why. We still call them out as you approach, because a new provider could switch them back on at any time without notice. Enforcement in Johannesburg also continues by roadblock and manned traps, so keep to the limit — it is the cameras that stopped, not the policing. Pretoria and Ekurhuleni run their own cameras and are unaffected.

items.title: Report a speed trap, and help keep it accurate
items.body: When you report a speed camera you can now say whether it’s a camera van or a permanent camera. Vans show on the map in amber for about three hours; tap one and tell us “still there” to keep it up for other drivers, or “not there” to take it down. Permanent cameras you report stay put — South African map data barely covers Gauteng’s fixed cameras, so those reports are genuinely valuable.

items.title: Your route appears immediately — safer options follow
items.body: Tapping Go now opens the route screen as soon as the standard route is ready, with a progress card showing the safer-route search still working. The safer options slide in when found — and if the search fails (weak signal), the screen says so instead of quietly pretending there was only one road. The search itself also retries once, so a brief signal drop no longer costs you the safer route.

items.title: An even-safer option, when going far around is worth it
items.body: Sometimes a much safer road exists but is too long for the normal detour limit. When it removes at least half the risk, it now appears as a separate "even lower-risk — much longer" card you can choose deliberately. It never replaces your route on its own, and one tap brings the shorter option back.

items.title: Safer routes will now go the long way around
items.body: When the direct road runs through high-risk areas, the Balanced and Safest options used to cap how far around they would take you — on some trips the only genuinely safer road was just past that cap, so all three options collapsed onto the same risky route. Escaping high-risk areas now earns extra detour room in proportion to the risk it removes, so a trip whose direct road crosses several danger zones can take the highway loop around them instead.

items.title: Lighter on memory during CarPlay drives
items.body: During a drive, up to five live maps could be open at once (the home screen and route screens stay loaded underneath navigation) — enough for iOS to shut the app down mid-drive on some days. Covered screens now release their maps while you navigate and bring them back the moment the drive ends, and the CarPlay dashboard tile falls back to its text card if the phone ever runs short of memory.

items.title: Road closures now follow the actual roads
items.body: A closed road used to be drawn as a short straight line through roughly the right spot, which cut across the street grid instead of tracing the road. Closures are now mapped along the real road, and the affected area is shaped around them rather than boxed off.

items.title: A road race is no longer flagged as a protest
items.body: Closures now say why the road is shut. A marathon or parade reads as a planned closure, roadworks as roadworks, and only actual unrest gets the red warning. You are routed around all of them the same way — the difference is what you are told.

items.title: Closures only apply while the road is actually shut
items.body: A closure announced days ahead used to start diverting traffic the moment it was added. It now stays dormant until its start time and clears itself when the road reopens.

items.title: More trustworthy closure data
items.body: The daily check that finds closures was quietly failing most mornings, and could place a road tens of kilometres away when the same street name exists elsewhere in the city. Both are fixed, and a road that cannot be pinned down is now held back for review instead of being guessed at.

items.title: CarPlay: the End button on your phone can no longer vanish
items.body: With CarPlay connected, switching the phone between the map and directions views (or tapping the trip stats) could hide the trip bar — leaving no way to end the route without force-closing the app. While CarPlay is connected the bar now stays put, always.

items.title: Locked-screen drives: music restore and rerouting hardened
items.body: On drives with the screen locked, the fix that hands your music back after each instruction could itself stop the background heartbeat that keeps the app responsive — leaving music dimmed and rerouting frozen until the screen woke. The hand-back now runs in the moment the spoken clip finishes, the background heartbeat repairs itself if it is ever paused, and the brief audio handover can no longer be interrupted midway.

items.title: New installs start with the full current risk map
items.body: The map data bundled into the app for a brand-new install was from the earliest days of Tsamaya — a handful of coarse blocks that showed for a few seconds until the live data downloaded. The app now ships with a complete, current copy of every zone and rated road, so the very first screen a new user sees is the real risk picture.

items.title: Android: smoother start to navigation
items.body: On Android, starting a drive no longer bounces you into the system settings page for background location — navigation starts immediately with while-you-use-it access.

items.title: Music really comes back after each instruction now
items.body: On CarPlay (and locked-phone drives) your music dimmed at the first spoken instruction and never recovered until you woke the phone. iPhones only restore other apps' volume when the app that dimmed them briefly lets go of the speaker — and Tsamaya was holding on for the whole drive to keep itself awake in the background. After each spoken line it now lets go for a split second and takes the speaker straight back: your music returns to full volume the moment the voice stops, and navigation keeps running with the screen off exactly as before.

items.title: The real reason directions kept going quiet
items.body: Every time Tsamaya finished speaking, it was handing the phone's audio back completely — which also gave up the permission it needs to keep running with the screen off. So after the first instruction of a drive it would gradually go to sleep, and only wake when you picked the phone up. It now keeps that permission for the whole trip. This is also what made your music jump back to full volume for a few seconds after each instruction.

items.title: Your music stays at full volume between directions
items.body: Music was being turned down for the whole drive instead of just while Tsamaya was speaking — dipping from the moment you set off and only coming back for a few seconds after each instruction. It now ducks around the spoken line and hands your music straight back.

items.title: Guidance no longer goes quiet mid-drive
items.body: This is the one that kept coming back. Tsamaya was asking iOS to let it keep running with the screen off, but iOS only grants that to an app that is actually playing sound — and between spoken directions there is none, so it kept getting put to sleep. It now plays a silent tone for the length of a drive, which keeps it awake and the directions coming. You will not hear it and your music is untouched.

items.title: Voice guidance keeps talking with the phone asleep
items.body: Directions could go quiet mid-drive and only pick up again the moment you woke your phone. Two separate causes: Tsamaya was letting iOS pause its own voice whenever the phone locked, and the claim it makes to keep running in the car was only made once when you plugged in — so if anything took it away later, nothing put it back. It now holds that claim for the whole drive and re-checks it as you move.

items.title: Better evidence if a drive ends by itself
items.body: If navigation ever stops without you ending it, the shared log now records why the screen closed and whether the drive was still running at the time — so the next report can name the cause instead of guessing at it.

items.title: Stops are announced by name
items.body: On a trip with stops, the voice used to say "you have arrived at your destination" at every stop — and then cut itself off mid-word. Each stop is now announced by its own name ("In 600 metres, Mall@55 will be on the left"), and only the real destination ends the trip. Reversing a trip with the swap button now also reverses your stops.

items.title: Road-closure alerts behave better
items.body: Dismissing a protest banner now hides only those closures — a new protest later in the day still alerts you. Alerts also stay quiet unless Tsamaya knows where you actually are, so you are never warned about another city’s roads.

items.title: Add stops along the way
items.body: Running errands? Tap "Add stop" on the route card to build a trip with up to four stops — shops, a friend, then home. Each leg is checked for danger zones separately, so the detour is as carefully routed as the main trip, and Tsamaya tells you when you reach each stop.

items.title: Protests and road closures
items.body: Tsamaya now watches the news each morning for planned protests, strikes and road blockades in your city, and routes you around them for as long as they last. Affected roads show as a red-and-white striped line, and you only hear about closures within 50 km of you.

items.title: The voice now finishes the drive
items.body: Arriving used to cut the guidance voice off mid-sentence — "in forty metres, you will arri—". Tsamaya now closes every trip properly: "You have arrived at your destination. Go well."

items.title: Full 3D maps on CarPlay — if you want them
items.body: A new switch in Settings › Navigation › CarPlay puts the full 3D map — buildings, landmarks and time-of-day lighting — on the car screens during the day. It is experimental and heavier on memory, so the proven flat driving map stays the default; after dark the high-contrast night map still takes over either way.

items.title: Your car, on the little dashboard map
items.body: The mini map on the CarPlay dashboard now shows your chosen vehicle marker — including your own uploaded car photo — instead of always the blue arrow.

items.title: Off the route, the risk readout reads where you actually are
items.body: When you left the route, the safety readout could keep reading the risk of the road you were supposed to be on rather than the one you are on. Once you are more than about forty metres off the line, it now reads your real position until the new route lands.

items.title: Two more ways the car could put Tsamaya back to sleep
items.body: Muting the voice mid-drive, or a genuinely stuck voice clip, could quietly undo the keep-awake fix from earlier today and return CarPlay to its slow-motion state. Both paths now leave the keep-awake alone.

items.title: Working out a route in the car is quick again
items.body: Tapping Home or Work on the car screen could sit on a spinner for over a minute and only finish when you woke your phone — a four kilometre trip took eighty seconds, of which the actual routing was about a fifth of a second. Tsamaya now keeps itself awake for your whole time plugged in, not just while a route is running, so working one out is as quick as following one.

items.title: The dashboard card stops going blank when you park
items.body: After arriving, the little card on the CarPlay home screen could drop back to "Open Tsamaya on the car screen" even though it was still running. One slow update was enough to make it give up on the whole session. It now holds on.

items.title: The road and its risk stay on screen while rerouting
items.body: While Tsamaya worked out a new route, the panel under your car replaced the road name and its safety rating with "Rerouting…". That is the moment you need it most — you have left the route, possibly somewhere you would rather not be. The road and its rating now stay put; the spinner says the rest.

items.title: The right speed limit for the stretch you are on
items.body: On a long run like the M1 the limit changes several times, but Tsamaya was showing one number for the whole stretch — and it picked the highest one, so a 100 zone displayed 120. It now reads the limit for the exact piece of road under your car. On the M1 north out of Rosebank that is 100 for most of it, as it should be.

items.title: Tsamaya keeps working while you drive
items.body: On a CarPlay drive your phone was giving Tsamaya almost no time to think — measured at four percent — which is why guidance arrived late, rerouting crawled, and the car screen only caught up when you picked the phone up. It now holds on to the audio channel it uses for spoken directions, which keeps it running for the whole drive. Your music is untouched.

items.title: The road rating matches the map again
items.body: The line under your car could be drawn green for a verified-safe road while the label beside it said "Unrated road". The map read the rating from the road itself; the label read it from your raw GPS position, which between tall buildings can sit a lane or two off. Both now read the road you are actually on.

items.title: A smaller road label on the CarPlay dashboard
items.body: The road name and safety pill on the little dashboard map were too big and sat low enough to hide behind the arrival time. Smaller now, and lifted clear of it.

items.title: The log stops calling restarts crashes
items.body: When you force-quit Tsamaya — to pick up an update, say — the navigation log recorded it as though the app had crashed, because it never got the chance to note it was closing. It now also records how long the app had been running and whether a real error was caught, so a restart no longer looks like a crash.

items.title: Rerouting actually finishes now
items.body: When you left the route, Tsamaya could sit on "Finding a lower-risk route" and then quietly give up — every time. The countdown it used to decide it had waited long enough kept running while the app itself was paused by the phone, so it had always "run out of time" before the new route had a chance to arrive. It now only counts time the app was genuinely awake and working.

items.title: No more two voices talking over each other
items.body: The natural voice and the built-in one could speak different instructions at the same time. Same cause as the rerouting problem: the app decided a clip had got stuck when really the phone had paused it, so it gave up and spoke the next instruction on top. Both now wait on time the app was actually running.

items.title: A bigger, tilted map on the CarPlay dashboard
items.body: The little Tsamaya card on the CarPlay home screen was mostly a text block, leaving only a sliver of map. Your speed is now the same round dial as the main screen, tucked into the corner, with the road name and its safety rating on a pill under the car — so almost the whole tile is map, and it is tilted to the same angle as the main navigation view.

items.title: The right road name in free drive
items.body: After ending a route, the car screen could name a house you were driving past rather than the road you were on. It now asks which road you are actually travelling along.

items.title: The route picker shows the route again
items.body: Choosing between Safest, Balanced and Fastest on the car screen zoomed out to fit the route across the whole display — including the half hidden behind the list of choices. It now fits the route into the part of the map you can actually see.

items.title: Better diagnostics when something goes wrong in the car
items.body: If you hit a problem while driving and share the navigation log from Settings, it now records far more of what happened: which part of the app failed, what was on screen over the map, and a much fuller crash trace. Nothing extra leaves your phone — the log still only goes where you send it.

items.title: CarPlay: your speed and road stay on the dashboard
items.body: The small Tsamaya card on the CarPlay home screen used to go quiet once a drive started, leaving only the posted limit. It now keeps your live speed, the road you are on and its safety tier for the whole drive, and the little map behind it is tilted to match the main one.

items.title: Risk areas now show on the car map
items.body: The CarPlay map drew flagged roads but not the risk area you were actually inside. Nearby zones are now outlined in their live colour, so an amber or red area is visible from the car screen too.

items.title: Route picker: a real Cancel, and a real overview
items.body: Choosing between Safest, Balanced and Fastest on the car screen now zooms out to show the whole route you are picking, and there is a clear ✕ to back out — instead of one unlabelled arrow in the far corner.

items.title: No more “Something went wrong” mid-drive
items.body: Picking up your phone while a CarPlay drive was already running could show a full-screen error. Fixed.

items.title: Discover — a guided flyover of your metro
items.body: Tap the new ✨ button on the map and Tsamaya flies you landmark to landmark through your metro — a tilted, cinematic tour of the places worth knowing, each with its quick guide and safety tip. Pause, skip around, or tap “Take me there” to route to any stop. Any pan or pinch hands the map straight back to you.

items.title: Landmark badges stay put, cards read in full
items.body: Landmark badges no longer vanish behind the map’s own labels as you zoom in, so they’re always there to tap. Their cards now scroll — the full guide and safety tip are readable, and long captions glide across instead of being cut off.

items.title: Discover the city — landmarks on the map
items.body: Iconic places across all seven metros now appear as small badges on the home map — Gold Reef City, Table Mountain, O.R. Tambo, the Union Buildings, Boulders Beach and dozens more. Tap a badge for a quick guide (what it is, how far, and the area’s risk read at this hour), then “Take me there” to route to it. Decorative only — landmarks never change your route. Turn them off in Settings › City landmarks.

items.title: The map opens flat
items.body: The home map now always opens in a top-down view — clearer for scanning zones at a glance. Tilt with two fingers whenever you want the 3D view; the map stays at the angle you set.

items.title: Flagged roads are no longer counted twice
items.body: Roads are stored as one row per carriageway (and a handful were accidentally saved twice), and route scoring summed every row — so a 3.1 km drive down a flagged road was counted as 6.5 km of risk, inflating its score and safety grade compared to roads stored as a single line. Every metre of a route now counts once, at the worst rating that covers it — the same way the map colours it. The 58 accidental duplicate rows were also removed from the dataset.

items.title: Route choice ignores flagged roads you aren’t on
items.body: Route scoring had the same blind spot navigation had this morning: a flagged road running right beside a safer highway (like the M1’s service roads) was counted against routes that never leave the highway — the M1 past Alexandra was scored as 4.5 km of medium risk that was 100% phantom, and roads you never touch could appear in the route’s caution list. The scorer now applies the same rule as the map and navigation: the road you’re actually on decides. Genuinely flagged roads (including split carriageways like "Main Road (west)") still count in full.

items.title: Safer highways stay green next to flagged roads
items.body: Highways marked as safer routes (like the M1 past Alexandra) were showing orange in navigation because flagged roads running right beside them — service roads, parallel main roads — sat close enough to bleed their risk onto the highway. The road you’re actually on now wins: a verified-safer road stays green unless the flagged road is the same road you’re driving. Area risk is unchanged — driving past a red zone still shows the zone and pulses the screen edge.

items.title: "Start Navigation" works again after cancelling a drive
items.body: Ending a drive and then starting a new route could leave the Start Navigation button doing nothing until you force-closed the app. Ending a drive quietly left the whole navigation screen alive behind the map (the system’s "go home" call stopped closing screens in a recent update), and the app’s guard against opening two navigation screens then blocked every new drive. Ending a drive now properly closes the screen — repeat trips start instantly, and the hidden screen no longer drains memory.

items.title: Allowed roads keep their true colour
items.body: If you tapped "Allow" on a higher-risk road on the route screen, navigation used to paint that road neutral blue ("Unrated road") — while the map and the corridor overlay still showed it orange, which looked like the app disagreeing with itself. Allowed roads and zones now always show their real risk colour on the route ribbon, the road readout and the car screen. Allowing still does what it promised: no detours around that road and no voice or vibration nagging — it just never hides the risk any more. Manage your allowed list in Settings › Routing › Allowed roads & zones.

items.title: Your voice choice is remembered
items.body: Choosing voice, alerts-only or silent on the car screen now sticks — the next drive starts in the mode you left it in, instead of resetting to full voice. The phone and CarPlay buttons also stay in step: change one and the other shows the same mode.

items.title: Your car photo survives app updates
items.body: The custom car marker no longer disappears after a new build. The photo was always kept on your phone, but the app remembered its location in a form that broke on every update — so you had to re-upload and re-size it each time. It now finds the photo again on its own, size and all.

items.title: Route colouring is ~30× faster
items.body: The coloured safety ribbon along your route is now computed with a spatial index instead of checking every mapped road for every stretch of the route. Long cross-town routes that took ~200 ms of freeze on every reroute now take a few milliseconds — on the phone and the car screen. The colours themselves are unchanged (verified point-for-point against the old calculation).

items.title: “Share without locations” now really does
items.body: Sharing diagnostics without locations was still including saved-place names (“Home”, your work) and the ids of hotspots you drove past. It no longer does — names, place ids and every coordinate are stripped, and the timeline, timings and journey times all stay. “Share full diagnostics” is unchanged and still includes everything.

items.title: The app now notices when it freezes
items.body: A heartbeat measures how late it runs, so a stall is recorded with the number of seconds it lasted instead of leaving a silent gap. Low memory is recorded too. If something goes wrong on a drive, the diagnostics you send will say what happened.

items.title: Rerouting no longer freezes the car screen
items.body: A mid-drive reroute now has a hard time limit, and the distance and arrival time keep counting down while it works. If it takes too long, Tsamaya simply keeps you on the route you are already driving and tries again shortly — the buttons on the car screen stay live throughout.

items.title: One voice at a time
items.body: When the phone and the car screen were both awake they could announce the same turn at once, in two different voices. Only one surface speaks now, and a prompt that gets cut short no longer leaves the next one waiting.

items.title: Home and Work from the CarPlay dashboard actually go
items.body: Tapping a dashboard shortcut now shows that it is finding your route, and tells you if something goes wrong instead of sitting there silently.

items.title: Ending a route ends it everywhere
items.body: Ending the drive on CarPlay used to leave the phone still showing turn-by-turn directions, so you had to end it twice. Now either one ends both.

items.title: Risk data loads once and is shared
items.body: Zone and road data is now read from the on-device cache a single time and shared with every screen, so plugging in CarPlay uses what the app already has instead of loading it all over again. Faster to start and much lighter on memory.

items.title: The map and the readout agree on the tier
items.body: Risky roads on the home map now follow the evening and night ratings the rest of the app already used, and the route line under your car carries a flagged road right to its end — matching what the readout says.

items.title: A flagged road stays flagged to its end
items.body: Risky roads are recorded in pieces, and those pieces can stop short of where the road actually ends. Drive past that point and the safety readout dropped to “Unrated road” while the map was still drawing the same road orange a few metres away. A road now keeps its rating across the join, so the words under the car and the colours on the map agree. It can only ever raise a warning, never lower one.

items.title: The CarPlay dashboard map actually moves now
items.body: The small map on the CarPlay dashboard used to be a still picture that refetched itself every several seconds, so it stepped forward in jumps and could not turn with you — the arrow pointed the right way while the map underneath lagged behind. It is now a real live map that scrolls and rotates continuously, like the one on the main car screen.

items.title: The speedometer works in slow traffic
items.body: Anything under about 9 km/h was being treated as a dead stop, so the speed read 0 while you were crawling in traffic. The filter that ignores GPS jitter on a parked car now cuts in at walking pace instead, so real crawling speeds show.

items.title: No more “No known risk” on a road we haven’t checked
items.body: When only the small built-in starter map was loaded — every road in it marked safe, none marked risky — the app could still tell you a road had “No known risk”, or call a flagged road “Unrated”. Glenhove Road, which is flagged in the live data, showed both. Whether the full risk data is really loaded is now judged from the data itself, so until it is, the app says it is still checking rather than guessing.

items.title: U-turn arrow points the South African way
items.body: The U-turn symbol was the right-hand-drive shape — looping to the left. In South Africa a U-turn crosses to the right, so the arrow is now mirrored to match what you actually do at the intersection.

items.title: Lock-screen distance keeps up
items.body: The distance to your next turn on the lock-screen card only refreshed every 15 seconds, so it sat well behind the car. It now updates whenever the number on it would actually change.

items.title: Speed limit always on the CarPlay tile
items.body: The posted speed limit now stays in the corner of the CarPlay dashboard map whenever there is one to show — driving a route or just driving around. It used to appear only during navigation.

items.title: Every screen tells the same story
items.body: While the risk data is still downloading on a fresh install, the route screen no longer says a route “avoids known risk areas” — it says the data is still loading, which is what the map and the drive were already saying. Same data, same answer, everywhere.

items.title: Green on the map means green
items.body: The driving map was drawing Mapbox’s own live-traffic lines, and their “traffic is flowing” colour is the same green Tsamaya uses for a road it has checked and rated safe — so ordinary roads with no safety rating at all could look verified. Those traffic lines are switched off on every map you tap, browse and drive with, so green there is a Tsamaya safety rating and nothing else. Traffic itself isn’t lost: while you’re driving, heavy and severe jams still show along your route in dark red.

items.title: A cleaner CarPlay dashboard
items.body: The mini map on the CarPlay dashboard no longer repeats the turn CarPlay is already showing. It now shows the speed limit in the top corner and a small pill under your car with the road you’re on and its safety tier — and it’s zoomed out a little and keeps moving smoothly instead of stalling between updates.

items.title: Freeway exits are named
items.body: Turn cards used to read just “Take the ramp” when a slip road had no name of its own. They now read “Take exit 26 onto M60”, using the exit number and road from the signs.

items.title: Honest about what we don’t know yet
items.body: Straight after a fresh install, before the full risk data finishes downloading, the road tier now reads “Loading risk data…” instead of calling every road unrated — and area warnings keep working throughout. The road name under your car is more honest too: through an interchange it used to keep naming the freeway you’d already left, right next to that road’s safety rating. It now reads the signposted route number off the ramp, and shows nothing rather than something stale.

items.title: Freeways route like freeways again
items.body: The N1, N4, N14 and the airport freeway through Joburg and Pretoria were being scored as risky roads, so routes were pushed onto slower surface streets to avoid them. About 330 km of national freeway now reads as the safe main route it is — the off-ramps and suburbs around them keep their own ratings.

items.title: Roads you draw get reviewed too
items.body: When you trace a road on the map, it now goes through the same AI review as every other report — and the reviewer can see what the app already knows about that spot, so it can tell a genuine gap from something already covered.

items.title: Send any place to Tsamaya
items.body: Got sent a location on WhatsApp, or found a place in another app? Tap Share → Tsamaya and it lands straight on your map, ready to route the safer way.

items.title: CarPlay, rebuilt under the hood
items.body: Guidance keeps flowing with your phone locked in your pocket, the car screen responds faster, and turn cards draw more smoothly — a set of deep native fixes from real-drive testing.

items.title: Faster, fresher maps
items.body: The map engine jumped several versions: quicker tiles, smoother offline handling, and groundwork for richer route colours.

items.title: Smarter drive diagnostics
items.body: The shareable navigation log now records CarPlay connects, map-style health, phone lock state and which screen is guiding — so field issues can be pinpointed from a single shared file.

items.title: CarPlay: big stability fix
items.body: Fixed the bug where plugging into CarPlay mid-drive could stack extra navigation screens (slowing everything down until the app crashed), and guidance now survives the car cancelling Apple’s turn cards — the drive keeps going instead of vanishing from both screens.

items.title: CarPlay map: never stuck blank
items.body: The car map now recovers by itself if the map style fails to load (bad signal at connect, or the evening style switch in a dead spot), and it runs a lighter, faster driving map built for car screens.

items.title: Cleaner CarPlay dashboard card
items.body: Our dashboard tile no longer duplicates Apple’s next-turn widget — it now sticks to what Apple doesn’t show: your speed, the road, its safety rating and your ETA.

items.title: Hey Siri, take me home
items.body: “Take me home in Tsamaya”, “take me to work”, “start navigation”, “end navigation” — Siri now works out of the box, no setup. Handy before you pull off or mid-drive.

items.title: Voice waits for your calls
items.body: Navigation prompts now pause automatically the moment a phone call starts and resume when you hang up — no more directions talking over your conversation.

items.title: Turns in your instrument cluster
items.body: On cars that support it, the next turn now shows behind the steering wheel — glyph, distance and road, coloured by road risk.

items.title: Volume slider now rules every voice
items.body: The guidance-volume slider now controls the device voice too (it previously only affected the natural voice). Diagnostics can also email support in one tap.

items.title: One-tap apply for drawn roads (admin)
items.body: Approving a hand-drawn road suggestion now matches it to the live road it follows and applies the rating to exactly the drawn stretch (start to end), or adds it as a brand-new road corridor when nothing matches — no manual editor work needed.

items.title: Draw the map you know
items.body: New pencil button on the home screen: outline an area or trace a road you know, rate how safe it is, and send it to us. The Tsamaya team and our AI reviewer check every suggestion before it changes anything — perfect for places where our street-level detail is still thin.

items.title: Natural voice by default
items.body: The natural-sounding guidance voice is now on for everyone (it was hidden behind a setting). If you’re offline it falls back to the device voice automatically — and you can still switch it off in Settings → Navigation.

items.title: Dashboard map moves with you
items.body: The CarPlay home-screen mini-map now glides continuously as you drive instead of jumping every few seconds, matches the day/night look of the main navigation map, and wears a coloured border when you are inside a risk area. While navigating it shows your speed, the road you are on and its risk level — the next turn stays in Apple’s own cards.

items.title: Music un-dims reliably
items.body: A voice prompt that got cut off could leave your music quiet until the next prompt. Volume now always restores within a second or two of a prompt finishing — or being interrupted.

items.title: Turns name the road, not the suburb
items.body: Spoken directions like “turn left toward Hatfield” now say the actual road — “turn left onto Gordon Road” — whenever the road name is known. Signposted ramps and forks still follow the signs.

items.title: Better diagnostics sharing
items.body: Share diagnostics now sends a small file covering the last 24 hours (not a month of text), including app version and settings — ready to attach to an email to admin@tsamayaapp.co.za.

items.title: Smoother map start-up
items.body: Risk zones and flagged roads now wait for the basemap to finish loading before they draw, instead of racing it — no more overlay glitches on launch or when the map look changes.

items.title: CarPlay dashboard map — actually there now
items.body: The map tile on the CarPlay home screen was showing black on real cars (an iOS map-engine limitation in that window). It now draws a live mini-map that follows you as you drive — rotating with your direction, zooming with your speed, and showing your route in its live safety colour when navigating.

items.title: CarPlay camera thinks in km/h
items.body: The head-unit map now zooms out as you speed up — highway driving shows the road ahead, not a close-up — leans back in for turns, and glides smoothly between GPS fixes instead of stuttering.

items.title: Your road, on the head unit
items.body: CarPlay now names the road you are driving — with its live safety colour — in both navigation and free drive, and the car sits offset from the turn cards like the big nav apps.

items.title: Dashboard widget works in free drive
items.body: The CarPlay dashboard tile now shows a live map, your speed, road and area safety even when Tsamaya is not open on the car screen — and it recovers by itself after long stops.

items.title: Paste any Google Maps link
items.body: Shared Google Maps links (maps.app.goo.gl and friends) now paste straight in as a destination — including shares that arrive as a place name plus a link.

items.title: Traffic alerts out of the way
items.body: The "heavy traffic ahead" notice no longer covers the road name and its safety level while navigating.

items.title: Live traffic, honest ETAs
items.body: Your ETA now reflects live traffic. Jams ahead show under the route line, and you get a heads-up when heavy traffic will cost you time.

items.title: Lane guidance
items.body: Lane arrows show which lane to be in for the next turn or exit — on your phone and on CarPlay.

items.title: Route safety grades
items.body: Every route now carries an A–E safety grade with a plain-language reason, so comparing routes takes one glance.

items.title: Beat the dark
items.body: Setting off late? Tsamaya now warns when you will arrive after dark — and how soon to leave to get in before it.

items.title: Know where you are heading
items.body: The destination card now reads the area itself — like “higher-risk area at night” — before you tap Go.

items.title: Report what you actually see
items.body: In-drive reports now use South African incident types — hijacking, smash-and-grab, spiking, blue-light stop and more. Two taps and it is filed.

items.title: Home and Work at a glance
items.body: Open the app and see a live ETA to Home or Work with a route risk chip — one tap to get going.

items.title: Sharper guidance
items.body: The camera now leans in for turns and eases out on straights, and the speedo warns you before the limit drops.

items.title: How did that area feel?
items.body: After a drive through flagged areas you can say how each one felt. Every answer tunes the safety map.

items.title: Speedo top-right in landscape
items.body: The speedo now sits in the top-right corner in landscape, with the buttons below it.

items.title: Landscape layout, sorted
items.body: In landscape the road name and safety pill sit under the car, the car rides a little higher, and the buttons keep clear of the screen edge.

items.title: Search follows you
items.body: Destination search now favours results near where you actually are — searching in Prague finds Prague, and full street addresses abroad resolve too. At home nothing changes: South African results still come first.

items.title: Tidier route panel
items.body: The “Roads on your route” chip no longer shows when there are no rated roads to list (for example outside covered metros).

items.title: Speed limits in free drive
items.body: The speed-limit roundel now works in free drive too — it previously only showed while navigating a route. Free drive matches your recent movement to the road you're on and reads its posted limit, wherever Mapbox has the data (including Europe).

items.title: Night colours back, 3D kept
items.body: Yesterday’s 3D-after-dark change accidentally swapped the home map’s night look away from the high-visibility night style — dimming the roads, zones and corridor colours. The night map is back to those colours, and the home screen now draws its 3D buildings on top of it, so you get both.

items.title: Offline maps
items.body: Download an area of the map for use without data — frame it, tap download, and it saves both the day and night looks. Your risk zones and safer corridors are already stored on your phone. Find it under Settings › Places › Offline maps. Search and routing still need a connection.

items.title: The map opens where you are
items.body: Opening the app away from home — another city or another country — now starts the map at your last known location instead of Johannesburg, and it no longer jumps back to Johannesburg during the day.

items.title: 3D buildings are back after dark
items.body: The home map keeps its 3D buildings when you tilt, at any time of day. Navigation still switches to the high-contrast night map while you drive — that one is about reading the road, not the skyline.

items.title: CarPlay dashboard 3D (experimental)
items.body: A new switch under Settings › Navigation renders the CarPlay dashboard widget on the full 3D map. Off by default — it uses more memory on the head unit, so try it and see how your car handles it.

items.title: Blue means unrated
items.body: Green now only means a road we’ve verified as safer. Roads we don’t have safety data for show in a neutral blue during navigation and free drive — on the route line, the road readout, and CarPlay — so an unrated road is never mistaken for a verified-safe one. Yellow, orange and red still mean what they always did.

items.title: Location arrow fixed
items.body: Fixed the iOS location indicator staying on after you’d finished with the app. Connecting to CarPlay no longer starts background GPS unless you’re actually navigating, and any stale background location from an earlier session is now cleaned up when the app opens.

items.title: Works anywhere now
items.body: Tsamaya now works as a normal map and turn-by-turn navigator wherever you are — even outside our covered metros or overseas. It centres on your real location and routes you normally. The safety layer (risk zones and safe corridors) still only applies where we have data, so routes outside coverage won’t avoid risk zones — the location pill shows your city tagged “(unstaged)” to make that clear.

items.title: Settings, tidied up
items.body: Settings is clearer and easier to find your way around. There’s a new Safety tab that gathers your risk alerts, crime hotspots and emergency contact in one place. The old “Time Band” control is gone — Tsamaya now adjusts risk automatically by the time of day, so there’s nothing to set.

items.title: Risk now follows the clock
items.body: Areas are treated as higher-risk from earlier in the evening — daytime runs to 5:30pm, evening 5:30–7:30pm, then night until 5am. The map’s evening and night look shifts at the same times, so what you see matches the risk. You can still pin the map’s look under Settings › Navigation if you prefer.

items.title: Road colour and area alert, shown separately
items.body: While navigating, the route now shows the ROAD’s own risk — a safe road stays green even through a high-risk area — and the glowing screen edge shows the AREA’s risk. So on a safe route through a red zone you see a green road with a red screen edge: you’re on the safe way through, and you can still see the area is high-risk.

items.title: Clearer maps in the evening too
items.body: The brighter, easier-to-read night map now kicks in from the evening — not just late at night — so roads stay clear as soon as it starts getting dark.

items.title: Safe routes still flag the most dangerous areas
items.body: On a safe route through a very high-risk (red) area, the road now shows an amber “stay alert” instead of green — so a red area is never shown as completely risk-free, even on the safe way through it.

items.title: A live map on the CarPlay dashboard
items.body: The Tsamaya card on the CarPlay home screen now shows a live map that follows you — like Maps and Waze — with your turn, ETA and safety colour floating over it. It works even before you set a destination.

items.title: Night maps are far easier to read
items.body: In dark mode and at night, the map now uses a purpose-built night-driving style — roads are bright and clearly visible (with highway numbers) instead of the near-invisible dark grey they were before. This applies to the home map and to turn-by-turn navigation.

items.title: Safe roads show as safe while you drive
items.body: A road we mark as a safe way through a risky area (a safe corridor, like the N3) now shows green while you navigate, instead of turning yellow or orange where it clips a flagged zone — matching how it already looks on the map.

items.title: Dangerous areas and dangerous roads now count equally
items.body: Safer routes now treat driving through a dangerous area as seriously as driving along a dangerous road of the same risk level. The router no longer cuts through a risky neighbourhood just to dodge a flagged road (or the other way round) — when the risk is equal, the shorter route wins.

items.title: Risky roads are always visible while you drive
items.body: Flagged higher-risk roads around you now show as coloured lines on the map during a drive AND in free-drive (no destination set) — on both the phone and CarPlay — so you can see the risk on the road you are on without needing a route.

items.title: CarPlay is smoother and clearer
items.body: Starting a drive from the car screen no longer sticks on “Loading…” or shows a doubled-up ETA, and the turn banner and speed no longer overlap. When a route ends the map keeps following you in free-drive, and the CarPlay dashboard card now fits without its ETA being cut off.

items.title: Speed reads zero at a standstill
items.body: The speed widget now drops to 0 promptly when you stop at a light instead of lingering on a low “creeping” number.

items.title: Guardian — one tap, someone watches over your drive
items.body: Share your Guardian link once (Settings › Navigation › Emergency contact), then tap the shield in CarPlay to let that person follow your drive live — they see your route, your live position, and the moment you arrive.

items.title: CarPlay: one-tap incident reporting
items.body: The report button now opens big one-tap buttons — Police, Crash, Hazard, Robot out, Smash & grab, Hijacking. One tap sends it to the review team without leaving your drive.

items.title: Risk data loads instantly on first run
items.body: A fresh install now uses the built-in risk snapshot immediately while the full live dataset downloads in the background — no more long "Loading risk data" wait at the start of a drive.

items.title: No more squashed car while panning
items.body: Panning away from the drive now flattens the map to a top-down view, so the car marker keeps its shape instead of being flattened by the 3D tilt. Re-centre returns to the chase view.

items.title: Tsamaya on the CarPlay dashboard
items.body: Tsamaya now provides the CarPlay home-screen navigation card — the live turn, ETA and safety colour show right on the CarPlay dashboard, with Drive home / Drive to work shortcuts. (Needs this new app version — update in TestFlight.)

items.title: Search destinations from the car
items.body: A new Where to? button on the CarPlay screen lets you search any destination on the car’s keyboard — plus your saved places and recent trips — and pick a Safest / Balanced / Fastest route without touching your phone. Route options now show the trade-off: “Avoids 2 risk areas · +4 min”.

items.title: Report speed cameras from CarPlay
items.body: The report button on the car screen can now add a permanent speed camera at your spot, with the limit it enforces — same review queue as the phone. Camera and hotspot voice alerts now play on CarPlay drives too.

items.title: Drives end themselves at the destination
items.body: A drive started from the car screen now ends itself when you arrive and stop — the map stays live with your safety colour, like a normal drive around town.

items.title: Lighter on long drives
items.body: Fixed the remaining memory growth when the route recalculates — long drives with lots of rerouting now stay smooth on phone and CarPlay.

items.title: Smoother, cleaner CarPlay
items.body: On CarPlay the map now glides continuously as you drive, instead of the car jumping forward once a second (and it rides on the road using the smooth route heading, not the jittery GPS one). The turn, ETA, safety and speed panels are now SafeNav’s own, arranged to stay clear of the car’s built-in controls.

items.title: Your car stays the right size
items.body: The vehicle marker now keeps a consistent size when you rotate to landscape or pan around the map — no more oversized car in landscape, and it no longer shrinks when you pan away to look ahead.

items.title: CarPlay safety colours match the map
items.body: On CarPlay, the route’s safety colours now follow the map’s day / evening / night lighting like the phone does, so an amber or red stretch reads clearly instead of looking washed-out on a dark evening map.

items.title: More accurate danger-zone edges
items.body: Zones drawn with a carved-out area (large farms or mines with an excluded patch) no longer treat that excluded patch as risky — the live safety readout now matches the exact zone shape shown on the map.

items.title: Lighter on long drives
items.body: Navigation now uses noticeably less memory while you drive, so a long trip stays smooth instead of slowing down or closing on you.

items.title: Smoother, freeze-free guidance
items.body: Navigation no longer briefly freezes when a voice prompt plays over Bluetooth or CarPlay, and guidance no longer falls behind and then fires a burst of turns at the intersection — you hear just the current instruction, on time.

items.title: Safety colours line up
items.body: The route line, the safety card and the screen-edge alert now always agree — an amber or red stretch shows the same everywhere, instead of a green road under an amber warning. The pulse only appears for genuine higher-risk areas.

items.title: Clearer turn wording
items.body: Roundabouts now read “At the roundabout, take the 1st exit”, and arrival reads “Arrive at your destination” — no more jumbled instruction text in the banner.

items.title: No more “Dropped pin” as your road
items.body: During a free drive, if we can’t name the exact road you’re on, the readout now keeps the last known road (or just shows the safety status) instead of labelling it “Dropped pin”.

items.title: Never shows “safe” before risk data loads
items.body: If the risk data hasn’t loaded yet (e.g. just after opening on a weak connection), the driving screen now shows a neutral “Loading risk data” state instead of a green “No known risk” — so you’re never told an area is safe when we simply don’t have the data yet.

items.title: Map always loads
items.body: If the map is slow or fails to load on a cold start, your route and car now appear anyway instead of a blank screen.

items.title: Crash reporting
items.body: If the app closes unexpectedly, Settings › General › Help & Feedback now offers to share what led up to it (locations removed) so we can fix it fast.

items.title: Drive opens centred on the route
items.body: When you start navigating, the camera now opens framed on the start of your route instead of off to the side — no need to pan and re-centre first.

items.title: Brighter route colour on dark maps
items.body: The live route line is a little brighter and clearer on the Evening and Dark maps.

items.title: Navigation starts where you are
items.body: If a route was built before your GPS had fully settled, navigation now re-anchors the start onto your real location instead of beginning elsewhere.

items.title: Route preview matches your map lighting
items.body: The route comparison screen now follows your Map lighting (Light / Evening / Dark) instead of always showing a light map.

items.title: Brighter colours on dark maps
items.body: Risk zones, roads and the live route now show clearer, brighter colours on the Evening and Dark maps so they no longer read muddy.

items.title: Voice volume slider
items.body: The guidance-voice volume is now a smooth slider (Settings › Navigation) instead of fixed steps, and quick changes no longer play two clips at once.

items.title: Size your own car marker
items.body: Uploading a photo of your car now keeps the whole image (no forced crop), with a Marker-size slider to fit it to the map. Your car also stays on screen when you pan the map during a drive, instead of switching to an arrow.

items.title: Clearer Evening & Dark maps
items.body: Risk zones and roads now read clearly on the Evening and Dark map styles, and switching the map lighting mid-drive no longer hides the car or route.

items.title: Tidier driving screen
items.body: The Re-centre button no longer overlaps the road name when you pan, and the safety readout now reflects the area you’re in, not just the road.

items.title: CarPlay: map or directions on your phone
items.body: While CarPlay is driving, tap Map / Directions on your phone to switch between the live map and the turn-by-turn list.

items.title: Choose your map lighting
items.body: Settings › Map & graphics › Map lighting now lets you keep the map matched to the time of day (Auto), or lock it to Light, Evening or Dark.

items.title: CarPlay refinements
items.body: On CarPlay: the speedometer (with the posted speed limit) now shows, the arrival card names your destination, distances read like Apple Maps (5 km / 600 m / 50 m), and your phone opens turn-by-turn directions automatically when a CarPlay drive begins.

items.title: A richer, time-of-day map
items.body: The map now uses Mapbox Standard with 3D buildings and lighting that shifts with the time of day — daylight, dusk and night. Phone feeling slow? Settings › Map & graphics has High / Balanced / Lite — Lite is the fast, flat map.

items.title: Tsamaya on CarPlay
items.body: Plug into a CarPlay car and Tsamaya guides you on the dashboard screen — the safer route, turn-by-turn, with your phone out of sight.

items.title: Keeps guiding with the screen off
items.body: Navigation now continues when your phone is locked or in your pocket — directions, voice and rerouting carry on in the background until you arrive.

items.title: More ways to make it yours
items.body: Use a photo of your own car as the map marker, rotate the navigation screen to landscape, and set the guidance voice volume — all in Settings.

items.title: Your route, coloured by safety
items.body: The route line now shows where it’s safer and where it isn’t — green along safer stretches, amber and red where it passes through higher-risk areas — so you can see the risk ahead at a glance instead of one colour for the whole trip.

items.title: Clearer voice directions
items.body: Guidance now names your next move earlier — “In 2 kilometres, take exit 10” instead of just “continue” — and tells you which side your destination is on as you arrive.

items.title: A safer-arrival summary
items.body: When you arrive, Tsamaya shows how many higher-risk areas your route steered you clear of — a quick note that the safer way was worth it.

items.title: Recent destinations
items.body: Tap “Where to?” and your recent places pop up straight away, so your regular trips are one tap from a route. They’re kept on your phone only.

items.title: Calmer, clearer guidance
items.body: Navigation no longer re-routes while you’re parked or after you’ve arrived, and voice prompts now wait their turn instead of talking over each other. Your destination shows a pin on the map, and arriving ends the drive cleanly.

items.title: Speedometer fixes
items.body: The speed dial turns red the moment you’re over the limit (even by 1 km/h), and snaps back to zero promptly when you stop instead of lingering.

items.title: Sharing polish
items.body: The share sheet opens instantly, and if you re-route mid-trip, anyone following your live link now sees your updated route.

items.title: A quick tour of the buttons
items.body: The first time you open the home, route and navigation screens, a short spotlight tour points out the key buttons — search, saved places, risk overlays, sharing, reporting and the SOS button. Replay it any time from Settings › Help › “Show me around”.

items.title: Support Tsamaya
items.body: Settings now has a “Support Tsamaya” option that opens our website if you’d like to help keep safer routing free. There’s never any pressure, and nothing is collected inside the app.

items.title: SOS now shares a live emergency link
items.body: Pressing SOS while driving texts your emergency contact your coordinates AND a “track me live” link they can follow for 24 hours. It’s location-only (no destination needed), keeps updating while you drive, and you can stop it any time — from the SOS button or a banner on the home screen.

items.title: Faster, smoother startup
items.body: The map’s risk overlays now load just after the app opens instead of during launch, fixing a brief freeze on startup (most noticeable in Low Power Mode).

items.title: Clearer risk info + tidier navigation
items.body: Ending a route returns you to the map. Risk labels are colour-based again (yellow = lower risk), tapping a zone explains it in plain language (“frequent reports of …”) instead of technical wording, and the in-drive buttons sit in a tighter group.

items.title: Shared trip links open straight in the app
items.body: Tap a shared Tsamaya link — a live trip, or a place someone sent you — and it now opens reliably inside the app, even when Tsamaya wasn’t already running. Before, a cold tap could land on a blank “unmatched” screen, and a live trip could briefly open over the wrong part of the world.

items.title: Clearer map: areas we haven’t rated yet
items.body: The map legend now spells out that a blank patch means “no risk data here yet” — not “assessed and safe.” A blank map is never a safety guarantee, so stay alert in unrated areas. Coverage keeps growing.

items.title: Share your drive, live
items.body: During navigation, tap Share › Share live location to send someone a link to your trip. They can follow your route and live position, see your ETA, and get an “Arrived safely” when you get there. It opens right in Tsamaya for anyone who has the app, or on the web for everyone else.

items.title: Live links close when you arrive
items.body: A shared trip link stops updating and shows that you’ve arrived once you reach your destination, then closes shortly after — so it can’t be used to track you later.

items.title: See why a road or area is flagged
items.body: The route screen now shows the reason behind each flagged zone or road — the local context we hold — so you can judge a detour for yourself, not just trust a colour.

items.title: Emergency contact is no longer hidden by the keyboard
items.body: Adding your SOS contact in Settings now scrolls the fields above the keyboard so you can see what you type. We’ll also remind you if a contact is missing its phone number.

items.title: Clearer turn directions
items.body: Fixed a turn instruction that could read twice (“Keep right toward Keep right…”), and the re-centre button now sits next to the road name instead of floating mid-screen.

items.title: A friendlier map and clearer wording
items.body: Dropped pins read as “Dropped pin” instead of raw coordinates, the route options use clearer “Lower-risk” wording, and the From/To card no longer overlaps the map buttons while you plan.

items.title: Better VoiceOver support
items.body: The map and navigation buttons now describe themselves to screen readers, with larger tap targets.

items.title: Lighter, faster map loading
items.body: Tsamaya now keeps your downloaded risk-zone and safe-corridor data between sessions and only re-fetches it when something has actually changed — so the map loads quicker and uses less mobile data each time you open the app.

items.title: Clear heads-up outside covered areas
items.body: Pick a destination outside Tsamaya’s covered metros and we now tell you plainly that the route is shown without risk avoidance — instead of quietly handing you an ordinary route.

items.title: Opt out of usage data
items.body: Settings › Privacy now has a “Share anonymous usage data” switch, so you can turn off the coarse, anonymous usage stats whenever you like.

items.title: Privacy policy updated
items.body: Our privacy policy now spells out exactly what optional live-trip sharing stores, and that you can have a shared trip deleted on request.

items.title: Crime hotspots on the map
items.body: Known hijacking and smash-and-grab spots now show as marked points with a risk circle, and you’ll get a spoken heads-up as you approach one while navigating. They’re NOT a complete list — coverage is growing and we’re still tightening exact locations. Turn them on or off in Settings › Navigation › Crime hotspots.
