items.title: Help place a hotspot correctly
items.body: Tap a hotspot, choose “Wrong spot?”, then tap its true location on the map to send a correction to our team for review.

items.title: More “Nearby” places
items.body: Nearby now also finds restaurants and tourist attractions, dropped as map pins with their star rating and whether they’re open now.

items.title: Add a speed camera’s limit
items.body: Tap a speed camera on the map to suggest its speed limit — handy for the Johannesburg cameras imported without one. Our team reviews each suggestion.

items.title: Share a navigation log
items.body: From Settings › General you can share a navigation log for diagnostics — with an option to trim the start and end so your home or work address stays private.

items.title: Hotspots line up with the road
items.body: Every hotspot was snapped to its real intersection or off-ramp using map road data, so the markers now sit where they belong instead of nearby.

items.title: Clearer risk-area alerts
items.body: Driving into a large higher-risk area now simply says “entering a higher-risk area.” The specific “hijacking / smash-and-grab” callout is reserved for the precise hotspot points.

items.title: Tidier “Nearby” pins
items.body: The “Clear pins” button moved below the quick actions so it no longer hides behind the search bar.

items.title: More reliable live location sharing
items.body: When you share your live location, the app now confirms the link is working before you send it — and “arrived safely” reliably shows when you finish your drive.

items.title: Voice directions on time
items.body: Spoken turn-by-turn now arrives on time even on a weak signal — if the natural voice can’t load quickly, it falls back to the on-device voice instead of going quiet.

items.title: Navigation arrow rides the road
items.body: The vehicle arrow now sits centred on your road instead of drifting off to the side.

items.title: Fixes & improvements
items.body: Added a “Check for app updates” button in Settings › General, sped up map-data loading, and stopped the “What’s New” card from repeating itself.

items.title: Flag a route that looks wrong
items.body: On the route screen, tap “Something off with this route? Send it to the team” to send us the proposed route and a note, so we can look into it.

items.title: Clearer route options
items.body: Each route’s dot now matches its colour on the map (Standard grey, Balanced green, Lower-risk blue). And when two options are the same road, we say so instead of quietly hiding one.

items.title: Never miss an update
items.body: You’ll now see a “What’s New” card after every update — and you can revisit the full history any time in Settings › General › What’s New.

items.title: Pick your route: Standard, Balanced or Lower-risk
items.body: Every trip now offers three routes — Standard (fastest), Balanced (avoids high-risk areas) and Lower-risk (avoids high + medium-risk). Choose per trip, or set a default in Settings › Default route.

items.title: Share your live location
items.body: From the navigation screen you can now share a live, trackable link so family can follow your drive in real time and see when you’ve arrived safely.

items.title: Find places nearby
items.body: Tap “Nearby” on the home screen to find the closest police station, hospital, fuel stop or mall and route straight there.

items.title: Safety nudges + SOS
items.body: Optional in-drive heads-ups for hijack / smash-and-grab hotspots, peak-risk times and arrival — plus an SOS button that alerts a chosen contact. Manage them in Settings › Safety.

items.title: Report speed cameras as you drive
items.body: Tap the report button while navigating to add a permanent speed camera at your spot. Our team reviews it — and it’s added automatically once a few drivers flag the same place.

items.title: Share your trip with family
items.body: Sharing a route now tells a friend where you’re driving from and to, your ETA, and any higher-risk areas you pass — so someone can keep an eye on your drive.

items.title: Speed cameras on the map
items.body: Known fixed speed cameras now show on the map, with a spoken “speed camera ahead” heads-up while you’re navigating. Turn it on or off in Settings › Navigation. (Coverage is best in Cape Town and still growing elsewhere.)
